extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, third parties submitting prior art, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements for (A) requesting redacted or voluntary publication of a U.S. patent application and (B) third-party preissuance submissions under 37 CFR 1.290. Covers timing, form, fees, document-listing, translation, and evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication — timing (16-month requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for redacted publication under 37 CFR 1.217 must be filed within sixteen (16) months after the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought under title 35, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 16-month period is statutory (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(v)) and requests for waiver of this 16-month period will be denied. If not timely filed, the Office will publish the full description as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication — required content (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for redacted publication must include: (A) a redacted copy of the application in compliance with USPTO electronic filing requirements; (B) a certified copy of each corresponding foreign-filed application; (C) a translation of each such foreign-filed application not in English and a statement the translation is accurate; (D) a marked-up copy showing the redactions in brackets; and (E) a certification that the redacted copy eliminates only the part/description not contained in any corresponding foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items (B)–(E) must be submitted in paper (including via USPTO electronic filing system) concurrently with the electronic submission of the redacted copy. The title in the redacted copy must correspond to the application title at submission. If the redacted copy does not comply with USPTO electronic filing requirements, the Office will publish the full description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication — format and filing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The redacted copy must comply with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements and any noncompliance will result in publication of the full description or refusal to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the redacted copy of the application does not comply with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements, the Office will publish the full description of the invention. Noncompliant requests may result in refund of publication fee but no publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication — fees and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission for redacted publication must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i) and the publication fee set forth in § 1.18(d) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that do not comply with requirements or electronic filing standards will not be published and the publication fee will be refunded. Papers submitted for redaction are not entitled to the certificate of mailing practice under 37 CFR 1.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary publication (37 CFR 1.221) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for voluntary publication of an application filed before but pending on November 29, 2000, or for republication of a previously published application must include a copy of the application in compliance with USPTO electronic filing requirements, the publication fee (§ 1.18(d)), and the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be pending when the request is filed. If the request does not meet USPTO electronic filing requirements, the request will be dismissed. The Office does not intend to publish abandoned applications; if the application becomes abandoned before publication, it may not be published even if the request was accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions — timeliness general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may submit printed publications of potential relevance if the submission is made in writing before the earlier of: (A) the date a notice of allowance is given or mailed, or (B) the later of (i) six months after the date the application is first published by the Office or (ii) the date of the first rejection under § 1.104 of any claim by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All third-party submissions must be filed prior to, not on, the listed dates. The time periods are statutory and cannot be waived; untimely submissions will not be entered or considered and will be discarded. Filing at the earliest opportunity is recommended, particularly where an initial submission is non-compliant and resubmission may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions — form (must be in writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third-party submission under 37 CFR 1.290 must be made in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel are instructed not to accept or act upon oral or telephone comments or submissions from third parties. Submissions not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.290 will not be entered into the application file and will be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions — required content (37 CFR 1.290(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each third-party submission must include: (1) a document list identifying documents or portions being submitted; (2) a concise description of the asserted relevance of each item; (3) a legible copy of each non-U.S. patent or non-U.S. patent publication item; (4) an English translation of any non-English item; and (5) a statement that (i) the party is not an individual with a duty to disclose under § 1.56 and (ii) the submission complies with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, submissions must include any required fee or the 1.290(g) statement claiming fee exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document list heading and page identification (37 CFR 1.290(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The document list must include a heading identifying it as a third-party submission under § 1.290 and identify on each page the application number of the application in which the submission is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)(i) and aids office processing; the web-based interface automatically generates the required format for electronic filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document list — separate sections for U.S. patents and other items
rubrics_metrics.description: The document list must list U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications in a separate section from other items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating U.S. patents/app pubs facilitates printing of considered U.S. patents and publications on the face of the patent. The electronic interface will automatically format the document list accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing requirements — U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. patent must be identified by patent number, first named inventor, and issue date. Each U.S. patent application publication must be identified by publication number, first named inventor, and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying by first named inventor helps locate items if document numbers are transposed or erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing requirements — foreign patents and published foreign patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each foreign patent or published foreign patent application must be identified by the country or patent office, the applicant/patentee/first named inventor, an appropriate document number, and the publication date indicated on the patent or published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(3) permits including applicant/patentee/first named inventor to aid identification in case of number transposition or other errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing requirements — non-patent publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each non-patent publication must be identified by author (if any), title, pages being submitted, publication date, and, where available, publisher and place of publication. If no publication date is known, provide evidence of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For internet sources, provide the URL of the web page and, where obtained from archived pages, provide both the archived page URL and the URL of the website from which the archived copy was obtained. If only part of a lengthy document is relevant, the third party may list only the relevant portion (e.g., one chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise description of asserted relevance (37 CFR 1.290(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise description of the asserted relevance of each submitted document must be provided; it should be a statement of facts regarding the submitted evidence and is not itself evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description can be in any format (narrative, claim chart) that best explains relevance. It is most effective when it draws the examiner's attention to relevant pages/lines, figures, or paragraphs of a lengthy document. The concise description should set forth facts explaining how the item is of potential relevance to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and translations of submitted items
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must supply a legible copy of each listed item except U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications, and must provide an English translation for any non-English item identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a non-English item is listed, include the translation and a statement that the translation is accurate. If a non-patent document has no clear publication date, include evidence of publication (e.g., retrieval date or archived web evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and fee exemptions (37 CFR 1.290(f)–(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party submission must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(o) for every ten items or fraction thereof listed. The fee is waived for a submission listing three or fewer total items if accompanied by a statement that, to the signatory's knowledge after reasonable inquiry, the submission is the first and only submission under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) filed in the application by the party or a party in privity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/429 allows indicating whether a fee is due or selecting the 'first and only' statement for the fee exemption. The fee amount and any exemptions are set by the Director and provided in § 1.17(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date, receipt rules, and holiday/weekend rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party submission is filed on its date of receipt in the Office as set forth in 37 CFR 1.6; the holiday/weekend rule of 37 CFR 1.7(a) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statutory filing date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day may be acceptable (e.g., via Priority Mail Express® or the Office's web-based interface). Certificate of mailing and transmission provisions of 37 CFR 1.8 do not apply to 1.290 time periods, but USPS Priority Mail Express® provisions under 37 CFR 1.10 do apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory nature of time periods and non-waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods in 37 CFR 1.290(b) are statutory and cannot be waived; third-party submissions not timely filed will be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-compliant submission does not toll the statutory period. A third party who files a non-compliant submission may file another complete submission provided the statutory time period has not closed. Abandonment of an application does not toll the statutory time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggering events for the timeliness windows
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6‑month time period is triggered only by publications 'by the Office' under 35 U.S.C. 122 and 37 CFR 1.211; publications by WIPO (e.g., PCT publication) or republication under 37 CFR 1.221(b) are not considered the 'first' Office publication for purposes of 1.290(b)(2)(i). The date of the first rejection under 37 CFR 1.104 that includes a rejection of any claim triggers the alternative time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filing does not reset the 1.290(b)(2)(ii) time period and does not preclude a third-party submission if the submission is made within the statutory periods. The filing of a notice of allowance controls timing where appropriate. Examples provided clarify that filings on the deadline date are untimely (must be before the date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling — noncompliant or unauthorized third-party communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office considers inappropriate any third-party inquiry or submission not provided for in 37 CFR 1.290 or 1.291; such submissions will not be entered and will be discarded. Office personnel should not reply to or act upon third-party submissions except those in compliance with 1.290 or 1.291.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should decline oral or telephone comments; when refusing such contact they may cite the statutory prohibition or 37 CFR 1.2 (business must be transacted in writing). Submissions by registered practitioners not in compliance may be referred to Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response to third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a request by the Office, an applicant need not reply to a submission under 37 CFR 1.290.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions are entered in the record for consideration by the examiner; applicants are not automatically required to respond unless the Office requests a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form PTO/SB/429 and electronic interface
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing in paper, third parties may use form PTO/SB/429 (or equivalent) to prepare the document list; electronic filing via the Office's dedicated web-based interface for preissuance submissions is an alternative and will auto-generate form PTO/SB/429 fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the form is not required for paper submissions but is designed to help ensure important requirements are not overlooked (document listing requirements, required statements, fee selection). For electronic submissions the interface prompts completion and automatically formats an electronic version of PTO/SB/429.
